title: Should we be designing our children?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with banter about the Science Channel's upcoming airing of Fringe and the movie Gattaca, then examine designer children: the Los Angeles fertility clinic that offered eye and hair color selection and faced public outcry, the UK bill on selecting embryos against disease or disability and the deaf community's protest, savior siblings, DNA and the Human Genome Project basics, preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) with IVF, transgenic animals and the spider-goat BioSteel example, and ethical concerns about genetic engineering and narrowing the gene pool. The episode closes with listener mail about Sandra Sroka and QSAC autism charity and Emily Eisenman's LifeStraw fundraising run.
topics: deaf community UK embryo selection bill

segments.title: Opening banter: Chevy Chase, Fringe and Science Channel
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Modern Problems and announce Science Channel's airing of Fringe, then introduce the designer children topic as a fringe science pick, mentioning Gattaca and a spoiler joke about Breaking Bad.

segments.title: Designer babies and the Los Angeles eye and hair color clinic
segments.summary: Hosts describe a Los Angeles fertility clinic that offered selecting eye and hair color, which drew public and international outcry and was withdrawn. They discuss how society may accept made-to-order children later.

segments.title: UK bill on selecting embryos and the deaf community protest
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a 2009 UK bill that would have allowed selecting embryos against disease or disability but not for deafness, which led the deaf community to protest. The bill also included savior siblings. They discuss whether deafness and Down syndrome are disadvantages.

segments.title: Savior siblings
segments.summary: Savior siblings are children conceived to act as donors for a sibling, such as umbilical cord blood saving an older sibling. The hosts debate how such children would be treated and their identity.
topics: ethics of conceiving children for donation

segments.title: DNA, genes and the Human Genome Project
segments.summary: Hosts explain DNA structure, nucleotides and base pairs, proteins and genes, junk DNA, chromosomes, and the 2003 completion of the Human Genome Project mapping.

segments.title: IVF and preimplantation genetic diagnosis
segments.summary: The hosts explain in vitro fertilization and preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD), which screens embryos for conditions such as hemophilia A and Down syndrome and raises the issue of gender selection, including in China.

segments.title: Transgenic animals, BioSteel and genetic ethics
segments.summary: Gene insertion is described as transgenic technology, with the spider-silk goat producing BioSteel as an example. The hosts discuss gene pool narrowing, unknown long-term consequences, moral obligations, and whether to choose traits like happiness.

segments.title: Listener mail: QSAC and LifeStraw fundraiser
segments.summary: A listener, Sandra Sroka, describes her work with QSAC, an autism services organization on Long Island and in New York City, and a bowling fundraiser. Another listener, Emily Eisenman, is running a thousand miles to fund LifeStraw purchases.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts recommend searching HowStuffWorks for genetics articles, mention the RSS feed, and give social media and email contact information.
